hints.title: Preserving All Base Employees
hints.text: Every employee from Employees must appear in the result set even if they lack a unique identifier.

hints.title: Left Outer Join Link
hints.text: left join EmployeeUNI on Employees.id = EmployeeUNI.id to retain null values where no unique identifier exists.

hints.title: Identifier Projection
hints.text: select EmployeeUNI.unique_id, Employees.name from Employees left join EmployeeUNI on Employees.id = EmployeeUNI.id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT eu.unique_id, e.name
FROM Employees e
LEFT JOIN EmployeeUNI eu ON e.id = eu.id;
```

complexity.notes: Hash join or index lookup on primary key id resolves in linear time proportional to table size.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: An inner join inadvertently discards employees who do not have an entry in EmployeeUNI.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Left join preserves all primary entity rows while emitting nulls for unmatched keys.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Standard left join preserving left-table cardinality.

solutions.approach: Left Outer Join on Employee ID

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def replace_employee_id(employees: pd.DataFrame, employee_uni: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = pd.merge(employees, employee_uni, on='id', how='left')
    return merged[['unique_id', 'name']]
